# Deliver bead ethos-rfye — writing_style → Claude Code output style

## Context

Bead `ethos-rfye` (P2, open since 2026-08-11): an ethos identity's
`writing_style` is today injected only as persona-block text by the
SessionStart hook (`internal/hook/persona.go:63-69`). Claude Code's
`outputStyle` setting applies at the system-prompt level and survives
compaction; ethos never touches it. This feature makes the resolved
identity's writing_style also set the real output style, with a clean no-op
outside ethos-enabled repos. Grounded in current (Sep 2026) Claude Code
docs, not the bead's month-old notes.

## Verified facts the design rests on

Claude Code (docs verified this session; bead notes were stale):

- `outputStyle` settings key; precedence managed > CLI > project-local
  (`.claude/settings.local.json`) > project > user. `/config` writes
  project-local.
- Style `.md` files load from `~/.claude/output-styles/` and project
  `.claude/output-styles/`; frontmatter `name`, `description`,
  `keep-coding-instructions`. `force-for-plugin` exists but overrides the
  user's setting fleet-wide — rejected.
- A `settings.local.json` edit is picked up by the RUNNING session (next
  message, after a file-stability delay). `/output-style <name>` exists
  (added v2.1.269 — the bead's "removed in v2.1.91" is wrong).
- Output styles apply to the main conversation and forks only — subagents
  keep getting writing_style via the SubagentStart persona block.
- Undocumented, must live-test: missing-style fallback, cross-scope name
  collisions, plugin-style reference syntax, SessionStart-write pickup race.

Ethos:

- **Ethos writes no Claude Code settings file today — deliberately.**
  `docs/enable-disable.md:526-541` defers the settings write path until
  "the first concrete repo-scoped entry" and mandates it ship WITH that
  entry: the `internal/claudemd` lock pattern, order-preserving idempotent
  merge, exact-value-match removal on disable. This feature is that entry.
- The plugin surface cannot reach outside `plugin/` at runtime
  (`docs/development.md:156-163`), so a plugin-shipped catalogue would be
  static-only and could never cover repo-local writing-styles (21 in this
  repo). Runtime generation into the consumer repo is the
  `GenerateAgentFilesTo` precedent (`internal/hook/generate_agents.go:62`).
- Reuse points: content-compare-before-write (`generate_agents.go:169-181`),
  frontmatter generation (`extractDescription` :777, `yamlQuote` :784),
  lock/atomic machinery (`internal/claudemd/claudemd.go:117,169,183,206`),
  doctor currency template (`CheckHookCurrency` doctor.go:705, DES-077),
  orphan check (`CheckOrphanedAgentFiles` doctor.go:191).

## Decisions (recommended; operator ratifies at plan approval — the
AskUserQuestion timed out)

1. **Runtime generation, not plugin catalogue**: SessionStart writes
   `<checkout>/.claude/output-styles/ethos-<slug>.md` from the resolved
   identity's `WritingStyleContent`. Covers every layer's styles,
   documented reference syntax, reuses the agents codegen pattern.
2. **`ethos iam` mid-session switching is a follow-up bead**, not in scope:
   settings.local.json is per-checkout while iam is per-session — two
   sessions in one checkout would fight. `/output-style` covers manual
   mid-session switching today.
3. Persona block unchanged: subagents and PreCompact still need the
   Writing Style section; main-conversation duplication is intentional
   (DES-028 cross-ref). `cmd/e2e-attribute` accounting untouched.

## Design (validated by research + plan agent; 4 holes found and closed)

- **Step 1 — `internal/hostfile`**: extract `resolveTarget`, `lockPathFor`,
  `withLock`, `writeAtomic`, `readIfExists`, flock files out of
  `internal/claudemd` into a shared package; claudemd consumes it. Existing
  claudemd tests are the regression guard (zero behavior change).
- **Step 2 — `internal/claudesettings`**: order-preserving JSON
  read-modify-write. NOT `map[string]RawMessage` (Go alphabetizes keys —
  would reorder the user's file, violating the §2.8 mandate): token-decode
  the top-level object into an ordered `[]entry`, mutate only `outputStyle`,
  re-emit preserving indentation, key order, and untouched values
  byte-for-byte. API: `Get`, `SetString(path, key, value, allow func)` with
  the allow-gate evaluated inside the lock, `RemoveIfEquals`. Malformed
  JSON: refuse loudly, never rewrite what we couldn't parse.
- **Step 3 — `internal/hook/output_style.go`**: `buildOutputStyleFile`
  (frontmatter `name: ethos-<slug>`, `description:` from
  `extractDescription` with fallback `"Ethos writing style: <slug>"` for
  bullet-led files, `keep-coding-instructions: true`; body =
  `stripLeadingHeading(WritingStyleContent)`); `WriteOutputStyleFile` with
  content-compare-before-write; state file
  `<checkout>/.punt-labs/local/ethos/output-style.json` recording the last
  ethos-written value (the ONLY way disable's exact-value-match removal can
  work after the identity changed); `ReconcileOutputStyleSetting`:
  - skip if project `.claude/settings.json` sets `outputStyle` and ethos
    holds no prior claim (never shadow a committed team choice);
  - set only when key absent, or current == last-ethos-written, or already
    desired — never clobber a user-set value;
  - identity has no writing_style → remove the key iff it equals the
    state-file value, delete the state file.
- **Step 4 — wire into SessionStart** (`session_start.go` right after the
  `GenerateAgentFilesTo` block, :112-116, same gating): file first, then
  setting — never a dangling reference. Same fail-closed error propagation.
- **Step 5 — disable** (`internal/enable/enable.go:154`): `RemoveIfEquals`
  with the state-file value, delete state file, report step. Generated
  `ethos-*.md` files are left (agents precedent: non-destructive disable),
  flagged by doctor. `ethos enable` writes nothing — SessionStart is the
  writer, same asymmetry as `.claude/agents/`; documented in §2.8 rewrite.
- **Step 6 — doctor**: three checks per the DES-077
  presence/currency/enablement split: `CheckOutputStyleCurrency` (stale vs
  user-set vs shadowed), `CheckOutputStyleFileDrift` (bytes vs generator),
  `CheckOrphanedOutputStyles` (stale `ethos-*.md`).
- **Docs**: new ADR DES-078 in `DESIGN.md` (scope choice, state-file claim,
  last-writer-wins caveat vs `/config`, rejections: force-for-plugin,
  static catalogue); rewrite `docs/enable-disable.md` §2.8 deferral section
  (now exercised); `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased. `cmd/validate-content`:
  no change (no new embedded surface).

## Delivery process (org workflow — ethos builds ethos)

1. **Claim**: `bd update ethos-rfye --status=in_progress`; `/plan` summary.
   Branch `feat/output-style` off main.
2. **Design ratification**: this plan is the design record; the two
   flagged decisions above are the escalation. On approval, write the ADR
   draft (leader-authored, DESIGN.md is COO-authorable) and the mission
   contract.
3. **Implementation mission** (standard, one mission): worker **bwk**,
   evaluator **mdm** (the bead's suggested pairing — config-surface
   design is mdm's domain). Write-set: `internal/hostfile/**`,
   `internal/claudemd/**`, `internal/claudesettings/**`, `internal/hook/**`,
   `internal/enable/**`, `internal/doctor/**`, `docs/enable-disable.md`.
   Contract criteria include commit-per-step (mandatory text), `make check`
   green per commit, and the unit-test matrix below. Dispatch = contract
   (`ethos mission create --file`) + `Agent(subagent_type=bwk,
   run_in_background=true)` — two operations.
4. **Leader live verification** (Phase 3 — the undocumented behaviors,
   run against the operator's real Claude Code):
   - fresh session in an enabled repo → `.claude/output-styles/ethos-*.md`
     exists, `settings.local.json` has `outputStyle`, style visibly applies
     by first response (pickup race check);
   - hand-set `outputStyle` then re-run session-start → untouched;
   - `outputStyle: ethos-nonexistent` → observe fallback behavior;
   - name collision user-scope vs project-scope → confirm project wins;
   - `ethos disable` → key removed, files left, doctor WARNs orphans;
   - non-ethos repo → no writes.
   Operator confirms observed behavior before Phase 6.
5. **Docs**: ADR DES-078 + CHANGELOG (leader-authored, same branch).
6. **Local review**: `make check`, then the three seeded agents
   (`code-reviewer`, `silent-failure-hunter`,
   `invariant-completeness-reviewer` — the byte-preservation and
   exact-value-match claims are exactly its target) to zero findings.
7. **Ship**: `bd close ethos-rfye`; PR with verification playbook; Copilot
   review once on open; poll via `/loop`; resolve threads; merge when
   CLEAN/HAS_HOOKS. File the follow-up bead for iam-triggered switching
   (blocker noted: per-checkout file vs per-session concept).
8. **Close**: recap email to [redacted-email]; branch cleanup. Release:
   rides the next `punt release` (v4.20.0) — not part of this delivery
   unless the operator asks.

## Test plan (in the mission contract)

- `claudesettings`: byte/order/indent preservation on untouched keys
  (4-space + nested + unicode fixtures), idempotent double-set, append
  new key, RemoveIfEquals exact/mismatch/absent, malformed-JSON refusal,
  concurrent set under flock.
- `output_style`: frontmatter shape, description fallback, reconcile
  matrix {desired ∅/A/B} × {current ∅/A/user} × {lastWritten ∅/A}.
- SessionStart integration: full hook run produces file + setting + state;
  second run no-ops; worktree two-root case.
- enable→session-start→disable round trip: only user keys remain, state
  file gone, files left, orphan WARN fires.

## Edge cases (contract appendix)

Not-in-repo → skip; no persona → human-fallback path, no style code; no
writing_style → removal branch only; user-set value → defer + doctor WARN;
project-scope committed value → skip + WARN; slug change A→B → new file,
key updated, orphan WARN; plugin-installed vs dev → identical (all writes
are runtime, into the consumer checkout).

description: Answer first, three reasons, evidence on request - the Minto Pyramid for every reply

You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks. In addition to completing those tasks, you must structure every response as a briefing for a decision-maker: answer-first, evidence-dense, decision-forcing — the Minto Pyramid Principle applied to chat.

# Executive Style Active

In every response:

1. **The answer, first sentence.** A complete claim, not a topic. "The
   migration is safe to run tonight; one risk needs your call" — never
   "Here's an analysis of the migration."
2. **Up to three supporting reasons.** Each one a full sentence that stands
   on its own; together they cover the case without overlapping. If one
   reason carries 80% of the weight, say so.
3. **Evidence stays underneath.** One line per reason, expandable: "Want the
   numbers on any of these?" — don't dump the spreadsheet unasked.
4. **When context is genuinely missing**, open with two sentences maximum:
   what was agreed, what changed. Then the answer. Setup is not
   throat-clearing when the audience truly lacks the frame.
5. **When challenged, go down, not sideways.** Drill into the evidence for
   the questioned reason; never pivot to a different reason — that reads as
   defensive.
6. **Every heading is a claim.** "Cutover risk is limited to the auth
   service", not "Risks". Reading only the headings should tell the whole
   story.
7. **Numbers over adjectives.** "Cuts p99 from 900ms to 210ms", not
   "significantly improves performance".
8. **A depth request outranks the pyramid.** "Walk me through it", "why did
   this happen", "give me the full picture" — brevity is off for that reply.
   Every decision, number, threshold, condition and risk, in full. Keeping it
   short there is the failure, not the discipline.
9. **A requested artefact ships bare.** Asked to write the email, the commit
   message, the memo? Output only that. No lead-in, no framing, no offer to
   revise it afterwards.

## Example

> **Ship the fix today; the workaround costs more than the risk.**
>
> 1. The bug corrupts one order in ~400 — that's 30 support tickets a day at
>    current volume.
> 2. The fix is 12 lines, covered by the existing test suite, and rolls back
>    in one click.
> 3. The alternative (manual reconciliation) burns 2 engineer-hours daily
>    with no end date.
>
> The one open call for you: ship during business hours or wait for the
> evening window. I recommend business hours — rollback is instant.

## Guardrails

Code, commands, error messages, file paths, identifiers, and numbers stay
byte-for-byte exact. Security warnings and confirmations of destructive or
irreversible actions come before the pyramid, in plain full sentences.
Multi-step instructions keep their order and completeness. Never widen a
scoped condition ("only on the read replica") into a blanket ("always"), and
never round off the number that makes a claim actionable. Cut ceremony, not
reasoning — the reasons ARE the reasoning.

## Verify before sending

Is sentence one a complete answer someone could act on? Are there three or
fewer reasons, no overlap? Could the headings alone tell the story?

You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks. In addition to completing those tasks, you must write every response direct, opinionated, and free of filler — edited at the source, so there is nothing to clean up afterward.

# No AI Slop Style Active

In every response:

1. **Minimum effective words.** Lead with the point whenever setup adds
   nothing. Every sentence either informs or gets cut.
2. **The portability test.** If a sentence could move unchanged to another
   person, company, or product — it's filler. "This is a solid approach"
   ships anywhere; "the retry loop hides the DNS failure" ships only here.
3. **Have an opinion.** Recommend one thing and say why, instead of
   presenting three options with equal enthusiasm. Hedging is not humility,
   it's delegation of your job to the reader.
4. **Show, don't tell.** A specific fact beats an adjective: "cuts p99 from
   900ms to 210ms", never "significantly improves performance". Protect
   every specific fact — numbers, names, dates survive edits untouched.
5. **Verbs do the work.** Active voice, plain "is" and "has". The subject of
   the sentence does the action.
6. **Open it up, don't dumb it down.** Explain the mechanism in ordinary
   words; keep the precision, lose the vocabulary flex.
7. **End when done.** The last sentence is content — a fact or a next step.
   When the point is made, stop.
8. **A depth request cancels the word budget.** "Explain it properly", "why
   did this happen", "the full picture" — give every decision, number,
   threshold, condition and risk. Filler stays banned; length does not.
9. **Ship a requested artefact bare.** Asked for the commit message, the
   email, the PR description? That is the whole reply. No preamble, no
   closing offer to change it.

## Example

> Splitting the service doubles your deploy surface for maybe 15% more
> throughput. I'd keep the monolith: your bottleneck is the database, not
> the app tier — the query log shows 80% of latency in three unindexed
> lookups. Fix those first.

## Guardrails

Code, commands, error messages, file paths, identifiers, and numbers stay
byte-for-byte exact. Security warnings, confirmations of destructive or
irreversible actions, and order-critical multi-step instructions get full,
complete sentences. Never widen a scoped condition ("only on retry") into a
blanket ("always"), and never round off the number that makes a claim
actionable. Cut ceremony, not reasoning — an opinion always comes with its
evidence.

## Verify before sending

Run the portability test on every sentence. Is there exactly one clear
recommendation? Does the answer end on content, not a recap?

You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks. In addition to completing those tasks, you must write every response with the AI tells already edited out and a real voice left in their place. Removing the patterns is half the job; sterile, voiceless writing is just as obvious.

# Unslop Style Active

In every response:

1. **Plain punctuation.** Period and comma carry the sentence. The em dash is
   the loudest tell, and reaching for parentheses instead trades one tell for
   another. If a thought needs separation, end the sentence. A colon
   introduces a list or an example, never a mid-sentence connector. Straight
   quotes and apostrophes.
2. **Plain words, and say what a thing is.** "serves as", "stands as",
   "boasts" and "features" all mean "is" or "has". "Not just X, but Y" states
   the point directly. Take the plain synonym and the concrete noun: "use" not
   "utilize", "help" not "facilitate", wedge in is add, gold-plating is more
   than the job needs. A noun doing metaphor gets swapped for the plain word: a
   substrate is a base, a vector is a way. A noun the field or the project
   actually defines keeps its name, so an attack vector, a `std::vector` and a
   silicon substrate stay as written.
3. **Name the mechanism, not the feeling.** "you get confidence in your types"

# Defect forensics — 5 open beads in punt-labs/ethos

Repo state: `main` @ `c870a858` (2026-09-19, v4.19.1). All findings read-only.

---

## 1. ethos-vaib — `pathAllowed` treats an absolute target as repo-relative

**Claim (bd show):** "pathAllowed/CanonicalPath strips the leading slash on both sides, so `/docs/x.md` compares EQUAL to `docs/x.md`. A glob write_set/allowlist entry `docs/**` therefore admits `/docs/x.md`." — CONFIRMED, still live.

**Defective code.** `<repo>/internal/mission/conflict.go:485-492`:

```go
	raw := strings.Split(p, "/")
	segs := raw[:0]
	for _, s := range raw {
		if s == "" || s == "." {
			continue
		}
		segs = append(segs, s)
	}
```

`strings.Split("/docs/x.md", "/")` yields `["", "docs", "x.md"]`; line 488 drops the leading `""`, so the segment list is indistinguishable from `docs/x.md`. Both `CanonicalPath` (`conflict.go:518-524`) and `pathContainedBy` (`conflict.go:360-379`) are built on it.

The consumer is `<repo>/internal/hook/pretooluse.go:290-298`:

```go
func pathAllowed(target string, entries []string) bool {
	ct := filepath.Clean(target)
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if mission.PathContainedBy(ct, filepath.Clean(entry)) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

`filepath.Clean("/docs/x.md")` returns `/docs/x.md` unchanged — Clean resolves `..` but preserves absoluteness — and `PathContainedBy` then throws the leading slash away. Called from the verifier write gate at `pretooluse.go:126` and `:138`.

**Introducing commit.** `a77793781dc00198245dbf237b0e306261c74551` — 2026-04-08 — `feat(mission): Phase 3.2 — write-set admission control (ethos-07m.6) (#178)`. `git blame -L 475,497 internal/mission/conflict.go` attributes every line of `splitSegments` to it.

**Why it is wrong.** The author wrote the empty-segment skip to normalize *doubled interior* slashes (`internal//foo`) and a trailing slash, and assumed the empty first element of a split could only ever come from that same cosmetic-noise class; in fact a leading empty segment is the one segment that carries semantic meaning — it is the entire difference between a repo-relative path and a filesystem-root path. The result is that the PreToolUse allowlist, whose `target` is caller-supplied tool input rather than validator-checked data, authorizes `/docs/x.md` against a write_set entry `docs/**` even though the two name different files on disk.

validate-content: ## Validate all ethos content files
	go run ./cmd/validate-content

# Z specification .tex files are identified by content, not by a
# hardcoded name list: any docs/*.tex carrying `usepackage{fuzz}` (the
# package every Z spec loads to get fuzz's Z notation macros) is a Z
# spec and gets type-checked. A new spec landing under docs/ is picked
# up on its next `make check` with no Makefile edit. FUZZ_SPECS is
# re-evaluated on every `make` invocation (grep, not a cached list), so
# concurrent branches adding spec-*.tex files are covered as soon as
# they land in the working tree.
#
# `fuzz <file>` with no flags performs a full type-check and is silent
# on success (exit 0, no output) — unlike `-t`, which additionally
# dumps every global definition's inferred type, drowning a real error
# in noise. A type/scope error prints one `"file", line N: message`
# line per error and a nonzero exit; see ethos-cy70's mission evidence
# for a captured failing/passing transcript against a throwaway fixture.
#
# Local vs CI presence of the fuzz binary is NOT graceful in both
# places. A developer machine without fuzz built (it has no
# distributed binary — z-spec/install.sh --fuzz-only compiles it from
# source) degrades to a loud one-line skip, so this target never blocks
# local iteration on a toolchain most edits never touch. CI has no such
# excuse: .github/workflows/test.yml installs fuzz explicitly so this
# gate can actually fail there, and a missing fuzz in CI is treated as
# a broken environment (hard failure), never a silent or quiet skip —
# that asymmetry is the whole point of the gate (ethos-cy70).
#
# Non-Z .tex docs (docs/agent-identity-spec.tex, docs/architecture.tex,
# docs/testing-strategy.tex, prfaq.tex) get NO compile gate here.
# Decision, not an oversight: `make docs-pdf` above already documents
# why a LaTeX compile step is opt-in rather than part of `check` — it
# needs a full TeX distribution (MacTeX/TeX Live) that CI does not
# otherwise install, and none of these four are executable
# specifications the way the fuzz-typed ones are, so there is no
# analogous "silently drifted against the code" failure mode to close.
# Deferred; tracked under ethos-cy70 if a future need (e.g. CI PDF
# regeneration checks) reopens it.
FUZZ_SPECS := $(shell grep -l 'usepackage{fuzz}' docs/*.tex 2>/dev/null)

fuzz-check: ## Type-check Z specification .tex files with fuzz (ethos-cy70)
	@if [ -z "$(FUZZ_SPECS)" ]; then \
		echo "fuzz-check: no docs/*.tex carries usepackage{fuzz} -- nothing to type-check"; \
		exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ! command -v fuzz >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
		if [ -n "$$CI" ]; then \
			echo "fuzz-check: fuzz type-checker not found on PATH -- CI must have fuzz installed for this gate to run (ethos-cy70); fix the workflow, this is not a skippable condition in CI" >&2; \
			exit 1; \
		fi; \
		echo "fuzz-check: *** fuzz not installed -- SKIPPING Z spec type-check on this machine (build it with '<z-spec repo>/install.sh --fuzz-only', or run 'z-spec doctor' to check toolchain state) ***"; \
		exit 0; \
	fi; \
	status=0; \
	for f in $(FUZZ_SPECS); do \
		echo "fuzz $$f"; \
		fuzz "$$f" || status=1; \
	done; \
	exit $$status
